7. Our question: metres to light-years (not from an exam paper) (3 marks)

Find the time in seconds first. Then turn the seconds into years.

Altair is 1.58 × 1017 m from Earth.

Calculate this distance in light-years.

Show the marking

Our answer, marked the SQA way. d = vt (1). 1.58 × 1017 = 3.0 × 108 × t, so t = 5.27 × 108 s (1). t = 5.27 × 108 ÷ (365.25 × 24 × 60 × 60) = 16.7 years, so 17 light-years (1).

8. Our question: metres to light-years (not from an exam paper) (3 marks)

Vega is 2.4 × 1017 m from Earth.

Calculate this distance in light-years.

Show the marking

Our answer, marked the SQA way. d = vt (1). 2.4 × 1017 = 3.0 × 108 × t, so t = 8.0 × 108 s (1). t = 8.0 × 108 ÷ (365.25 × 24 × 60 × 60) = 25.4 years, so 25 light-years (1).

Answers

Say it the exam way

(1) distance · (2) year · (3) 3.0 × 10⁸ · (4) d = vt · (5) seconds · (6) 640 years · (7) past

2024 Section 1, Question 8: answer D

  • A Not this one. II is right, but III is right too: the Big Bang theory describes the origin of the Universe.
  • B Not this one. III is right, but so is II: the Universe is about 13.8 billion years old.
  • C Not this one. I is wrong. A light-year is a distance: how far light travels in one year.
  • D Right. II and III are true. I is wrong: a light-year is the distance light travels in one year, not a time.
  • E Not this one. I is wrong. A light-year is a distance, not a time.

2024 Section 1, Question 6: answer D

  • A Not this one. This uses the speed of sound (340 m s−1). Laser light travels at 3.0 × 108 m s−1.
  • B Not this one. This divides the speed by the time. Use d = vt: multiply.
  • C Not this one. This divides the speed by half the time. Use d = vt: multiply 3.0 × 108 by 1.3 s.
  • D Right. The light goes there and back, so the time one way is 1.3 s. d = vt = 3.0 × 108 × 1.3 = 3.9 × 108 m.
  • E Not this one. 7.8 × 108 m is the distance there and back. Halve the time first.
